GENERIC_NO_DISPLAYS: No displays detected. Please connect a display to your PC.
GENERIC_NO_COMPATIBLE_DISPLAYS: No compatible displays found. Please check that "DDC/CI" is enabled for your displays.
GENERIC_DDC_WARNING: DDC/CI features can cause your monitor to become unresponsive. Use at your own risk.
PANEL_TV_MIRROR_NOTE: Mirroring {{1}}, so dimming affects both screens. Use Extend to give the TV its own desktop.
PANEL_TV_AUTO_NOTE: Disconnected while the TV is off. It reconnects when the TV turns on.
PANEL_TV_AUTO_SHORT: Reconnects when the TV is on
PANEL_TV_UNAUTHORIZED: The TV no longer accepts this app. Pair it again in Display Control settings.
PANEL_TV_API_DOWN: Turning it off, volume, mute and Ambilight are unavailable. They come back on their own once the TV responds.
PANEL_TV_SLEEP_FAILED: The TV didn't turn off when Windows went to sleep ({{1}}).
PANEL_TV_SHUTDOWN_FAILED: The TV didn't turn off when Windows shut down ({{1}}).
INTRO_INSTRUCTIONS: The tray icon for Twinkle Tray is probably hidden, so you should move it to some place you can easily access it. See below for instructions.
SETTINGS_NIGHT_LIGHT_TIP: Sets Night Light's strength on all displays. 0 hands it back to Windows, which means off, or its schedule if you have one. Windows has no official way to do this, so an update could stop it working.
SETTINGS_NIGHT_LIGHT_UNAVAILABLE: Night Light's settings aren't in a format this app recognizes, so the slider is hidden and they're left unchanged.
SETTINGS_NIGHT_LIGHT_PER_DEVICE: This PC also has a per-device copy of these settings, which the slider doesn't change. If moving the slider has no effect, Windows is probably using that copy.
SETTINGS_NIGHT_LIGHT_PER_DEVICE_SHORT: May not work on this PC
SETTINGS_TV_PAIR_DESC: Turn the TV on first to get a PIN
SETTINGS_TV_NOT_FOUND: No TV found. Check it's on, or enter its address.
SETTINGS_TV_PIN_EXPIRED: The PIN expired. Press Pair to get a new one.
SETTINGS_TV_WAKE_DESC: Wakes the TV after you log in
SETTINGS_TV_WAKE_TIP: Needs Twinkle Tray to open at startup, and "Switch on with LAN" turned on in the TV's settings.
SETTINGS_TV_STANDBY_TITLE: Turn off when Windows shuts down
SETTINGS_TV_STANDBY_TIP: The TV goes off even if you're watching another input on it.
SETTINGS_TV_SLEEP_DESC: Off when it sleeps, on when your screens return
SETTINGS_TV_SLEEP_TIP: Also applies to hibernating. The TV stays off if the PC only wakes briefly in the background, or if it was already off.
SETTINGS_TV_SCREENS_OFF_TITLE: Turn off when your screens turn off
SETTINGS_TV_SCREENS_OFF_TIP: Waits this long first, so a brief screen-off doesn't turn it off. It stays on while a TV app or the home screen is showing. It can't tell HDMI inputs apart, so a console on another input would be turned off too.
SETTINGS_TV_SAVER_TITLE: Keep the TV's screen saver away
SETTINGS_TV_SAVER_DESC: Sends an arrow key every 4 minutes while screens are on
SETTINGS_TV_SAVER_TIP: Also sends one when your screens wake. This turns off the TV's protection against static images while your screens are on, which is a burn-in risk. A TV app or menu in use may see the key.
SETTINGS_TV_AUTO_TITLE: Disconnect its display when it turns off
SETTINGS_TV_AUTO_DESC: Stops windows getting stuck on the TV
SETTINGS_TV_AUTO_TIP: Windows can't tell when a TV goes to standby. This moves windows to your other screens, then reconnects the display when the TV turns on. Chromecast must stay enabled on the TV, as that's how the app tells when it's on.
SETTINGS_DISPLAYS_DIM_DESC: Dims the picture with an overlay
SETTINGS_DISPLAYS_DIM_TIP: Works in HDR and for displays without brightness control, but not over exclusive fullscreen apps.
SETTINGS_DISPLAYS_HDR_DESC: Same as Use HDR in Windows
SETTINGS_DISPLAYS_HDR_TIP: The screen may flicker while it switches.
SETTINGS_DISPLAYS_BLACKOUT_TIP: Covers the screen with black while windows stay where they are. Click the black screen to bring it back.
SETTINGS_DISPLAYS_MODE_TIP: A new mode goes back to the old one after 15 seconds unless you keep it, in case it leaves the screen without a picture.
SETTINGS_LAYOUTS_DESC: Save and restore your display setup
SETTINGS_LAYOUTS_TIP: Saves which displays are on, where they sit, and their resolution and refresh rate, so you can switch back in one click or with a hotkey.
SETTINGS_API_DESC: For scripts and automation on this PC
SETTINGS_API_TIP: Controls displays and the TV. It can't be reached from other devices, and every request needs the token.
SETTINGS_GENERAL_BRIGHTNESS_STARTUP_DESC: Restore the last known brightness for each display when Twinkle Tray starts.
SETTINGS_GENERAL_DISABLE_ON_LOCK_SCREEN_: Don't access monitors while the user session is locked to avoid conflicts in multi-user environments.
SETTINGS_GENERAL_RESET_DESC: Hit this button to clear your config.
SETTINGS_GENERAL_ACRYLIC_DESC: Enable or disable the blur behind transparent backgrounds in Twinkle Tray.
SETTINGS_GENERAL_MICA_DESC: Enable or disable the blur behind backgrounds in Twinkle Tray.
SETTINGS_GENERAL_SCROLL_DESC: Adjust the brightness of all displays at once by scrolling over the system tray icon. This does not work with some trackpads.
SETTINGS_GENERAL_DIS_MONITOR_FEATURES_DE: If Twinkle Tray is unresponsive when clicking on the tray icon or not detecting your displays, you can try disabling certain monitor detection methods. Restart Twinkle Tray for changes to take effect. {{1}}
SETTINGS_GENERAL_OVERLAY_DESC: How forcefully the brightness hotkey overlay will attempt to display over other apps. You should not need to adjust this.
SETTINGS_GENERAL_DIS_OVERLAY_DESC: If Twinkle Tray's hotkey overlay is interfering with fullscreen applications, you can disable it here.
SETTINGS_GENERAL_ON_OVERLAY_DESC: The overlay will display over most windows, but will not force itself above apps that are marked as "always on top".
SETTINGS_GENERAL_FORCE_OVERLAY_DESC: Always try to show the overlay on top of other windows. This can cause issues with exclusive fullscreen games and other fullscreen apps. It can also trigger anti-cheat in some games.
SETTINGS_GENERAL_LEGACY_DDC_DESC: Use the old v1.15.5 method of detecting DDC/CI displays.
SETTINGS_GENERAL_AUTOBRIGHT_DESC: If your monitor responds strangely after turning it off/on or disconnecting/connecting hardware, disabling this may help.
SETTINGS_GENERAL_SKIP_APPLY_DESC: Disable auto-applying known brightness after all hardware/power events for specific monitors. This include the idle detection feature.
SETTINGS_GENERAL_REPORT_DESC: Save a text file with information about your monitors and settings for debugging.
SETTINGS_GENERAL_SKIP_THEME_CHANGES_DESC: Detects accent/wallpaper/theme changes from Windows to update the tray icon and Mica effect. Disabling this may help if a 3rd party app is frequently changing the theme, increasing CPU usage.
SETTINGS_GENERAL_SKIP_POWER_EVENTS_DESC: Detects changes to the power state of monitors. Disabling this may help if you experience errors when monitors are turned off/on or are idle. Requires a restart to take effect.
SETTINGS_MONITORS_RATE_DESC: How often the brightness will be updated on your displays as you're adjusting their values. Increase the time if your displays are flickering.
SETTINGS_MONITORS_RENAME_DESC: If you'd prefer a different name for each monitor (ex "Left Monitor", "Middle Monitor"), you can enter it below. Leaving the field empty will restore the original name.
SETTINGS_MONITORS_REORDER_DESC: Change the order that monitors are displayed in the tray. Click and drag to make changes.
SETTINGS_MONITORS_NORMALIZE_DESC: Monitors often have different brightness ranges. By limiting the min/max brightness per display, the brightness levels between displays is much more consistent.
SETTINGS_MONITORS_CALIBRATION_DESC: Each monitor can have individual calibration points added to compensate for differences in brightness curves. The input value is the brightness level indicated on the slider, while the output value is the actual brightness level applied to the monitor.
SETTINGS_MONITORS_HIDE_INTERNAL_DESC: When the lid is closed or the internal display has been disabled in Windows, hide the brightness slider in the panel.
SETTINGS_MONITORS_HIDE_DISPLAYS_DESC: If you would like to hide specific displays from the flyout, you can toggle them off here.
SETTINGS_MONITORS_HDR_DISPLAYS_DESC: Enable SDR brightness sliders for specific monitors. The monitors must have HDR enabled in Windows for this to work.
SETTINGS_MONITORS_GAMMA_SLIDER_DESCRIPTI: If your display does not support standard brightness control, you can use this as an alternative.
SETTINGS_MONITORS_EXTEND_MINIMUM_DESCRIP: The low end of the slider adds extra dimming
SETTINGS_MONITORS_EXTEND_MINIMUM_TIP: The percentage is how much of the slider this uses. In that part, the display stays at its lowest brightness and a dark overlay does the rest. It also works in HDR, but doesn't reach exclusive fullscreen games.
SETTINGS_MONITORS_EXTEND_MINIMUM_BREAKPO: Share of the slider used for extra dimming
SETTINGS_MONITORS_GAMMA_HDR_UNAVAILABLE: Not available while HDR is on
SETTINGS_MONITORS_SDR_SLIDER_DESCRIPTION: Control SDR brightness from main brightness slider while HDR is active.
SETTINGS_FEATURES_DESCRIPTION: Enable or disable specific DDC/CI features in the brightness panel. At least one feature must be enabled for your monitor to show up in the brightness panel. Not all displays support these features, such as laptop/tablet displays.
SETTINGS_FEATURES_UNSUPPORTED: This monitor does not support DDC/CI features.
SETTINGS_FEATURES_CUR_BRIGHTNESS_DESC: Always get the latest values from the monitor when opening the brightness panel. Enable this if the brightness (or other VCP codes like contrast) frequently change from outside of Twinkle Tray.
SETTINGS_FEATURES_POWER_DESC: When sending the DDC/CI command to turn off your display, the following value(s) will be sent.
SETTINGS_FEATURES_POWER_WARNING: The "Standby" option is more likely to allow toggling the monitor on/off from Twinkle Tray. However, many monitors do not respond correctly to changing power state. Use at your own risk.
SETTINGS_FEATURES_DDC_BLOCK_DESC: Stop Twinkle Tray from sending any DDC/CI commands to specific displays. Use this for displays that slow down or freeze your system when probed, such as those connected through one-way optical HDMI cables, or adapters that don't pass DDC/CI through. Applies to all connected displays of the same model, and blocked displays can't be controlled over DDC/CI.
SETTINGS_FEATURES_ADD_DESC: Enter the VCP code for the feature you would like to add to your display. Please note that Twinkle Tray does not validate if your display actually supports this VCP code. Use at your own risk.
SETTINGS_FEATURES_VCP_LIST_TITLE: All VCP codes reported by this display
SETTINGS_FEATURES_VCP_LIST_DESC: The following is a list of available VCP codes reported by this display to Windows. Twinkle Tray does not validate the functionality or stability of these VCP codes. Use them at your own risk.
SETTINGS_FEATURES_DDC_MAXIMUM_DESC: Use this if the display reports an incorrect maximum volume. Leave blank to use the reported value.
SETTINGS_FEATURES_BRIGHTNESS_VCP_INFO: If your monitor uses a non-standard VCP code for brightness (such as 0x13 or 0x6B), or if you would like to remap the brightness slider to a different VCP code, you can enter that code below.
SETTINGS_FEATURES_BRIGHTNESS_VCP_DESC: Leave empty for default (0x10). Find supported codes in the list below.
SETTINGS_TIME_DESC: Automatically set your monitors to a specific brightness level at a desired time. All monitors will be set to the same, normalized levels.
SETTINGS_TIME_INDIVIDUAL_DESC: Configure the brightness per display instead of for all displays at once.
SETTINGS_TIME_TRANSITON_DESC: How quickly brightness should transition when time of day adjustments are activated.
SETTINGS_TIME_STARTUP_DESC: Adjust the brightness to match the most relevant time when Twinkle Tray starts.
SETTINGS_TIME_IDLE_DESC: When no input has been detected for a period of time, the brightness of all displays will be reduced.
SETTINGS_TIME_ANIMATE_DESC: Brightness values will be animated between the current and next scheduled event. May increase CPU usage. Manual brightness adjustments will quickly be overwritten while this is active.
SETTINGS_TIME_SUN_DESC: To use "sun position" for time adjustments, enter your current latitude and longitude so the correct times can be determined.
SETTINGS_TIME_IDLE_FS_DESC: Fullscreen apps block idle detection. This only applies to the focused window.
SETTINGS_TIME_IDLE_MEDIA_DESC: Idle detection will be disabled while any media is playing. This includes both video and audio. This only applies when Windows reports that media is playing.
SETTINGS_HOTKEYS_DESC: Configure hotkeys to adjust the brightness of one or all displays.
SETTINGS_HOTKEYS_NATIVE_BRIGHTNESS_WARN: Windows will still adjust the built-in display when a brightness key is pressed. Do not use a BrightnessUp or BrightnessDown hotkey to adjust the built-in display's brightness.
SETTINGS_HOTKEYS_NATIVE_BRIGHTNESS_CHECK: A checkmark only means Twinkle Tray is listening for brightness keys. Many laptops handle these keys in firmware, so they never reach Twinkle Tray. Press the key to make sure the hotkey works.
SETTINGS_HOTKEYS_LEVEL_DESC: How much the brightness should be adjusted when using hotkeys.
SETTINGS_HOTKEYS_INVERT_SCROLL_DESC: When scrolling over the system tray icon, the scroll direction will be reversed.
SETTINGS_HOTKEYS_TOD_DESC: Customize the signal sent when using the Turn Off Displays hotkey or icon. The software signal will display a black screen until input (ex. mouse or keyboard) is detected by Windows. The hardware signal will turn off power to the monitors.
SETTINGS_HOTKEYS_TOD_NOTE: *Note: Not all DDC/CI monitors support this feature.
SETTINGS_HOTKEYS_BREAK_DESC: When using a hotkey for a single display and "linked levels" is active, it will be deactivated.
SETTINGS_HOTKEY_OFF_WARN: This action will use the option selected under "Turn Off Displays action". If you wish to turn off specific displays instead, use the "Set" or "Cycle" Hotkey Action instead.
SETTINGS_PROFILES_DESC: Automatically adjust the brightness or shortcut overlay behavior depending on the focused app. You can also add profiles to the right-click menu in the system tray to quickly change the brightness to pre-defined profiles.
SETTINGS_PROFILES_APP_DESC: If you want this profile to activate automatically when a specific app is focused, enter the full or partial path of the EXE below.
SETTINGS_PROFILES_OVERLAY_DESC: Changes the behavior of the hotkey overlay when the specified app is focused. This feature does not work when the profile is manually activated.
SETTINGS_LIGHT_SENSOR_DESC: Automatically update the brightness based on environment light from a light sensor.
SETTINGS_LIGHT_SENSOR_TYPE_DESC: Choose the type of light sensor to use.
SETTINGS_LIGHT_SENSOR_POLLING_DESC: Set the interval at which the sensor polls for light data.
SETTINGS_LIGHT_SENSOR_MONITORS_DESC: This maps each monitor's brightness (0%-100%) to ambient light levels in Lux. For example, setting the range to 5 and 250 means:
SETTINGS_LIGHT_SENSOR_MONITORS_DESC_MIN: When the sensor reads 5 Lux or less, brightness is set to 0%.
SETTINGS_LIGHT_SENSOR_MONITORS_DESC_MAX: When the sensor reads 250 Lux or more, brightness is set to 100%.
SETTINGS_LIGHT_SENSOR_MONITORS_DESC_INTE: Values between 5 and 250 Lux are linearly interpolated.
SETTINGS_LIGHT_SENSOR_FAKE_DESC: A fake sensor for testing purposes. Set the simulated light level below.
SETTINGS_LIGHT_SENSOR_FAKE_LUX_DESC: Set the simulated light level in Lux.
SETTINGS_LIGHT_SENSOR_WINDOWS_DESC: Uses the Windows built-in ambient light sensor to automatically adjust brightness.
SETTINGS_LIGHT_SENSOR_WINDOWS_NOT_FOUND: No Windows ambient light sensors found
SETTINGS_LIGHT_SENSOR_YOCTO_DESC: Get environment light from a Yocto light sensor.
SETTINGS_LIGHT_SENSOR_YOCTO_INSTALL_DESC: To communicate to the sensor, you need to install the "Yocto Virtual Hub" this allows this program to talk to connected sensors on your pc
SETTINGS_LIGHT_SENSOR_YOCTO_AUTOSTART: The virtual hub can be configured to auto start by running it on the command line with '-i'
SETTINGS_LIGHT_SENSOR_YOCTO_SERVICE: See "-i : Installation as a service" here
